g.text: Diffusion transformers (DiT) (Peebles & Xie, 2023) have achieved notable
success in image (Chen et al., 2023; 2024b; Esser et al., 2024) and video
generation (Ma et al., 2024a; Zheng et al., 2024; PKU-Yuan Lab and Tuzhan AI
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=7) Diffusion transformers (DiT) (Peebles & Xie, 2023) have achieved notable success in image (Chen et al., 2023; 2024b; Esser et al., 2024) and video generation (Ma et al., 2024a; Zheng et al., 2024; PKU-Yuan Lab and Tuzhan AI etc., 2024), attracting significant attention for their potential.

g.text: Although iterative denoising, classifier-free guidance (CFG) (Ho & Salimans,
2022), and transformer attention mechanisms have significantly improved the
generative capabilities of diffusion models, they also lead to substantial…
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=1) Although iterative denoising, classifier-free guidance (CFG) (Ho & Salimans, 2022), and transformer attention mechanisms have significantly improved the generative capabilities of diffusion models, they also lead to substantial computational costs and increased memory requirements for inference, especially for video generation which typically takes 2-5 minutes to synthesize a 6-second 480P video, limiting their practical use.

g.text: This calls for the development of new techniques that require less
computational cost for diffusion models (Salimans & Ho, 2022; Ma et al.,
2024b; Chen et al., 2024c; Zhao et al., 2024c).
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=4) This calls for the development of new techniques that require less computational cost for diffusion models (Salimans & Ho, 2022; Ma et al., 2024b; Chen et al., 2024c; Zhao et al., 2024c).

g.text: Among the recently proposed solutions, cache-based acceleration has emerged
as one of the most widely adopted approaches.
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Among the recently proposed solutions, cache-based acceleration has emerged as one of the most widely adopted approaches.

g.text: This approach speeds up the sampling process by reusing intermediate
features across timesteps, thereby reducing redundant computations and
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) This approach speeds up the sampling process by reusing intermediate features across timesteps, thereby reducing redundant computations and significantly improving computational efficiency.

g.text: Besides, it requires no additional training costs for inference acceleration
and offers straightforward generalization to other video diffusion models.
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Besides, it requires no additional training costs for inference acceleration and offers straightforward generalization to other video diffusion models.

g.text: Examples include cache-based methods for U-Net based diffusion models (Ma et
al., 2024b; Li et al., 2023b), residual caching in ∆-DiT (Chen et al.,
2024c) for transformer based diffusion models, and hierarchical attention
g.title: N7 [Prior_Work] (cites=4) Examples include cache-based methods for U-Net based diffusion models (Ma et al., 2024b; Li et al., 2023b), residual caching in ∆-DiT (Chen et al., 2024c) for transformer based diffusion models, and hierarchical attention caching of PAB (Zhao et al., 2024c) for video generation.

g.text: Despite their proven effectiveness, there exist two critical concerns:
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) Despite their proven effectiveness, there exist two critical concerns:

g.text: 1) Whether directly reusing intermediate features aligns with the
iterative denoising mechanism, considering the inherent feature

g.text: 2) Current cache-based methods focus primarily on the attention

g.title: N8b [Limitation] (cites=0) 2) Current cache-based methods focus primarily on the attention features within the transformer networks, with limited exploration of accelerating different parts of the pipeline.

g.text: In this work, we aim to address these two concerns.

inference for video generation, we delve into the feature reuse
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) To thoroughly investigate the acceleration potential of DiT inference for video generation, we delve into the feature reuse process of existing cache-based methods.

g.text: Existing methods assume high adjacent-step similarity

of feature similarity between adjacent timesteps in the iterative
denoising process, and achieve accelerated inference by sharing
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) As shown in Fig. 2, these methods typically assume a high degree of feature similarity between adjacent timesteps in the iterative denoising process, and achieve accelerated inference by sharing features across consecutive timesteps.

g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) However, our investigation reveals that while features in the same attention module (e.g., spatial attention) appear to be nearly identical between adjacent timesteps, there exist some subtle yet discernible differences.

g.title: N18 [Result] (cites=0) In contrast, the similarity of unconditional features between adjacent timesteps is relatively weak.

g.text: We further discover that the differences between the conditional and

g.title: N19 [Result] (cites=0) We further discover that the differences between the conditional and unconditional outputs are predominantly concentrated in low- to mid-frequency features during the mid-sampling phase, shifting to high-frequency features in the late-sampling phase, with these differences evolving gradually.

g.text: Based on the above insights, we propose a novel strategy, termed
FasterCache, to accelerate the inference of video diffusion models
while ensuring high-quality generation and remaining
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=0) Based on the above insights, we propose a novel strategy, termed FasterCache, to accelerate the inference of video diffusion models while ensuring high-quality generation and remaining training-free.

g.text: Specifically, we first introduce a dynamic feature reuse strategy
for attention modules which dynamically adjusts the reused
features across different timesteps, ensuring both distinction and
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) Specifically, we first introduce a dynamic feature reuse strategy for attention modules which dynamically adjusts the reused features across different timesteps, ensuring both distinction and continuity of features between adjacent timesteps are maintained.

g.text: This strategy preserves the subtle variations essential for the iterative
denoising process while ensuring temporal consistency, resulting in
accelerated inference with minimal loss of details in the generated videos.
g.title: N22 [Method] (cites=0) This strategy preserves the subtle variations essential for the iterative denoising process while ensuring temporal consistency, resulting in accelerated inference with minimal loss of details in the generated videos.

g.text: Furthermore, we introduce CFG-Cache, an innovative technique that stores the
residuals between conditional and unconditional outputs, dynamically
enhancing their high-frequency and low-frequency components before reuse.
g.title: N23 [Method] (cites=0) Furthermore, we introduce CFG-Cache, an innovative technique that stores the residuals between conditional and unconditional outputs, dynamically enhancing their high-frequency and low-frequency components before reuse.

g.text: This significantly accelerates inference while preserving details in
g.title: N24 [Method] (cites=0) This significantly accelerates inference while preserving details in generated videos.

(PKU-Yuan Lab and Tuzhan AI etc., 2024), Latte (Ma et al., 2024a),
g.title: N25 [Result] (cites=5) We evaluate our FasterCache on various video diffusion models, including Open-Sora 1.2 (Zheng et al., 2024), Open-Sora-Plan (PKU-Yuan Lab and Tuzhan AI etc., 2024), Latte (Ma et al., 2024a), CogVideoX (Yang et al., 2024), and Vchitect-2.0 (Fan et al., 2025).

g.text: Fast + high quality across all models
As shown in Fig 1, experimental results demonstrate that
FasterCache can significantly accelerate inference while
preserving high-quality video generation across all tested models.
g.title: N26 [Result] (cites=0) As shown in Fig 1, experimental results demonstrate that FasterCache can significantly accelerate inference while preserving high-quality video generation across all tested models.

g.text: Specifically, on Vchitect-2.0, FasterCache achieves 1.67× speedup,
with performance comparable to the baseline (VBench: baseline
g.title: N27 [Result] (cites=0) Specifically, on Vchitect-2.0, FasterCache achieves 1.67× speedup, with performance comparable to the baseline (VBench: baseline 80.80% → FasterCache 80.84%).

g.text: Beats baselines on both speed and quality
Furthermore, our method outperforms existing approaches in both
inference speed and video generation quality, highlighting its
effectiveness and efficiency in real-world applications.
g.title: N28 [Result] (cites=0) Furthermore, our method outperforms existing approaches in both inference speed and video generation quality, highlighting its effectiveness and efficiency in real-world applications.

g.text: We analyze the feature reuse process in cache-based
methods and discover that while adjacent-step features
in attention modules appear to be similar, their subtle
differences can degrade output quality if ignored.
